bug_semantics: With nltk.pathsec.ENFORCE True, a caller-supplied corpus root still reaches raw filesystem I/O in named constructors. LinThesaurusCorpusReader(root) calls CorpusReader.__init__ then builtins.open() on abspaths under that root; PanLexLiteCorpusReader(root) skips super().__init__ and sqlite3.connect(os.path.join(root, "db.sqlite")). pathsec.open blocks the same outside path, so this is a sandbox bypass (CWE-73) of the NLTK data-root policy, reading arbitrary files or SQLite databases.
flaw_origin: The CWE-73 sinks are constructor-derived paths used without pathsec validation. LinThesaurusCorpusReader was first added in 2eabeab4114c047649175487d8c97bc2d7f16b69 with super().__init__(root, r"sim[A-Z].lsp") then with open(path) on self.abspaths(); parent 37aaec359272789122119dbfaefc17f4116ed85f has no lin.py. PanLexLite independently first bound sqlite3.connect to a caller root in ab8305f6ca297b70731181af89764772eb334c61 (parent used os.environ["PANLEX_LITE"] / hardcoded db.sqlite). pathsec (4386e344, ENFORCE default True in 155e403) never validated CorpusReader roots or these sinks. 10d34b3f later routed Lin through pathsec.open (CWE-59) on develop but not in v3.10.2. Direct fix bc007200 validates string/FileSystemPathPointer roots in CorpusReader.__init__ and PanLex db_path via validate_path(required_root=root).

reasoning: The published bug is constructor-supplied corpus roots reaching builtin open/sqlite3.connect outside the pathsec data sandbox. Those sinks were first written when LinThesaurusCorpusReader was added in 2eabeab4114c047649175487d8c97bc2d7f16b69: new file, raw open() on paths derived from the constructor root, parent tree has no such reader. That is a single-parent first-write, not a move/refactor/squash. PanLexLite later independently introduced the sqlite join(root) sink (ab8305f6) without super().__init__; it is a second first-write of the same constructor-root CWE-73 class, not a smaller BIC than Lin. pathsec and ENFORCE=True are later incomplete retrofits, not first-writes of the unsafe I/O. The commit that actually closes GHSA-3gq4 is bc007200 (root validation in CorpusReader.__init__ plus PanLex validate_path), which lands in 3.10.3 and is absent from 3.10.2.
